name: spheroid-invasion
title: Tumor spheroid invasion
question:
Can the wrapper reproduce an invasive-growth morphology in CompuCell3D — a
proliferating core that expands with a rough, fingering front rather than a smooth
disc — driven through the Process config?
hypothesis:
A proliferating cell population with adhesion and surface parameters that favour an
extended interface expands as an invasive front: cell count grows and mean cell
surface rises faster than for compact growth, reflecting a rougher boundary.
objective:
Seed 25 cells on a 150x150 lattice, advance 4000 Monte-Carlo steps through
`CompuCell3DProcess`, and track population and mean surface through the output ports.
description:
An invasion demonstration: a small seed proliferates into a large, spreading mass
whose front is rough rather than smooth. The run is a single real cc3d 4.6.0
trajectory; the committed scene shows the expanding, fingering morphology.
claim:
The wrapper reproduces an invasive-growth morphology on the real engine: the
population expands from 25 to 675 cells over 4000 MCS while mean cell surface rises
from 22.3 to 44.1 px — a near-doubling that signals the rough, extended invasive
front rather than a smooth compact disc.
expected_behavior: Mean cell surface rises markedly (rough, extended front).
The animated scene shows an invasive, fingering boundary rather than a smooth disc.

readouts.name: Mean cell surface
readouts.description: Rises 22.3 -> 44.1 px, reflecting the rough invasive front.

readouts.name: Invasion morphology
readouts.description: Fingering, expanding front shown in the committed animated scene.

behavior_tests.name: Invasive proliferation morphology on the real engine
behavior_tests.description:
The invasion composite runs on cc3d 4.6.0 through the single-Process wrapper and
produces a proliferating core with a rough, expanding front (committed animated
scene + population/surface charts).

limitations: Surface growth is used as a proxy for front roughness; a dedicated invasion metric (e.g. radius-of-gyration or boundary fractal dimension) is a natural follow-up.

blocked_by: Invasive proliferation morphology on the real engine
